validity.researcher_notes: ADJUDICATED: P0146 (Alaska Pipeline Project) and P0174 (Denali - The Alaska Gas Pipeline) are TWO GENUINELY COMPETING PROPOSALS, not one physical project entered twice. Two independent origins say so explicitly. (1) Office of the Federal Coordinator, arcticgas.gov: 'Denali-The Alaska Gas Pipeline, a joint venture of North Slope producers ConocoPhillips and BP, was established in April 2008 TO COMPETE WITH the TransCanada project ... In May 2011, Denali announced it would no longer pursue development.' (2) CRS R40963: 'the State of Alaska's 2008 award to TransCanada ... and the concurrent announcement of a COMPETING pipeline proposal, the Denali project, by BP and ConocoPhillips. Through 2010, the Denali and TransCanada pipelines were proceeding along similar tracks. However, in May 2011, Denali's developers announced the discontinuation of their pipeline project'. They differ on every axis that identifies a project: SPONSORS (TransCanada + ExxonMobil vs BP + ConocoPhillips); REGULATORY VEHICLE (AGIA license awarded Dec 2008 + FERC pre-file Docket PF09-11-000 vs a non-AGIA proposal with its own separate FERC pre-file); CAPACITY as proposed (CRS: TransCanada 4.5-5.0 Bcf/d; Denali 4.0 Bcf/d); SCOPE (Denali always included its own gas treatment plant, the AGIA project initially did not); and END DATE (Denali withdrew May 2011; APP's prefile docket was terminated 26 Aug 2014). They shared an origin (Prudhoe Bay), a corridor (the Alaska Highway route to Alberta) and a rough design scale, which is why the rows look alike. CAVEAT and the reason this is not a clean 'none': P0146's Capacity and Length [ref] cells currently cite a Hart Energy article about DENALI's cancellation - a cross-row misattribution that made the two rows look like one. Both are re-pointed to APP-specific sources in fills[]. A second-order concern for P0174 (raised as a cross-row lead, not edited here): CRS states Denali was a 4.0 Bcf/d proposal, while GEM carries 4,500 MMcf/d on that row, so the identical capacity that prompted the duplicate suspicion may itself be an artifact of the same misattribution.

summary: Alaska Pipeline Project (TransCanada/ExxonMobil AGIA, Prudhoe Bay-Caroline AB) exists, is correctly classified as a cancelled transmission line, and is NOT a duplicate of P0174 Denali (BP/ConocoPhillips) - two independent federal sources call them competing proposals; headline defect is LengthKnownUnits 'km' where every source says 1,700 MILES; 4,500 MMcf/d, 48 in, 2500 psig, 26bn USD 2009 and CancelledYear 2014 all confirmed, with Capacity and Length re-pointed off a Hart Energy article about Denali.

verifications.note: FERC Nineteenth Report to Congress under ANGTA, February 2015: 'On August 26, 2014, TC Alaska filed with the Commission its intent to terminate the prefile review process for the Alaska Pipeline Project in Docket No. PF09-11-000'; 'The Alaska Pipeline Project's pre-filing docket has been terminated, and thus there is no progress to report.'

Office of the Federal Coordinator (arcticgas.gov) Alaska natural gas pipeline project history, Wayback 2015-09-08: 'ExxonMobil announced June 15, 2009, it had joined with TransCanada under the name Alaska Pipeline Project'; open season closed May 2012 with no shipper agreements; 'The state and TransCanada in summer 2014 ended their AGIA relationship'; Denali was 'a joint venture of North Slope producers ConocoPhillips and BP ... established in April 2008 to compete with the TransCanada project'.

Interior Gas Utility reprint of Matt Buxton (Fairbanks Daily News-Miner), June 2014: Gov. Parnell 'we have terminated the license with TransCanada under AGIA' — the state-side end of the Alaska Pipeline Project.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: CONFIRM. The Alaska Pipeline Project is cancelled and stays cancelled. Dated federal evidence: FERC's Nineteenth Report to Congress under ANGTA (February 2015) records that on 26 August 2014 TC Alaska filed its intent to terminate the prefile review process in Docket PF09-11-000 and concludes 'The Alaska Pipeline Project's pre-filing docket has been terminated, and thus there is no progress to report.' The Twentieth Report carries no APP section. Corroborated by the Office of the Federal Coordinator (state and TransCanada ended the AGIA relationship in summer 2014) and by Alaska press (Gov. Parnell, June 2014: 'we have terminated the license with TransCanada under AGIA'; Fairbanks Daily News-Miner via Interior Gas Utility; also Alaska Public Media 2014-06-19, which states the same but does not name the project so is not staged as a ref). The Alaska gas-export effort did not stop in 2014 - it moved to the Alaska LNG / Nikiski project (GEM P0147, a different route to a different terminus) - but that is a successor project, not a revival of this row. ShelvedCancelledType 'confirmed' and CancelledYear 2014 both hold. No Status change proposed; nothing in this review contradicts the Status fill.
